subject: Subprocessor roster + encryption ownership for SOC 2 / SIG review
messages:
From: Alice Hu <alice.hu@medalign.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>; camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medalign.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Subprocessor roster + encryption ownership for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Jonas / Camila,

As part of our SOC 2 scoping and SIG intake for our upcoming vendor review, we need a current subprocessor roster that includes: name, service provided, data types (customer content / telemetry / metadata), locations, and the encryption responsibility (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed keys).

Could you also confirm the following items for our security team:
- Who is the KMS key custodian for hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deploys?
- Which subprocessors have access to plaintext customer content (if any)?
- Any controls or evidence (matrix, controls mapping) that tie subprocessors to SOC 2 control IDs or SIG questions.

Deliverable target: ideally by Thu, Dec 23 so we can include in the audit packet. If you have a CSV + a short mapping doc that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Alice Hu
Security Program Manager
MedAlign Health
alice.hu@medalign.com
- Attachment: none
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Hu <alice.hu@medalign.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor roster + encryption ownership for SOC 2 / SIG

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a CSV and a short responsibility matrix. Two quick clarifying items so we scope the output correctly:

1) Data classification: do you want us to split "customer content" into subtypes (PII, PHI, model inputs/outputs) or is a high-level tag (Customer Content | Telemetry | Metadata) sufficient for MedAlign's intake?
2) Residency / onshore requirements: do you need us to flag subprocessors that operate within US-only regions (we can add a residency column)?

We will prepare: a subprocessor roster CSV and a KMS responsibility matrix that maps hosting mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) to key ownership, rotation ownership, and where applicable, HSM/KMS provider. Camila will attach the files once I validate the final rows.

Jonas Weber
Security Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
- Attachment: none

Hi Alice — forwarding the roster and matrix Jonas referenced. Quick highlights up front:

- Attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026-12-21.csv (columns: subprocessor_name, service, data_types, regions, access_level, encryption_ownership)
- Attached: kms_responsibility_matrix_2026-12-21.pdf (maps Hosted / Dedicated / Private -> key owner, rotation owner, provider)

Summary of key points for SOC 2 intake:
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed KMS by default (AWS KMS primary; GCP KMS for models hosted in GCP regions). Keys are rotated on a 12-month cadence; Redwood is the custodian.
- Dedicated capacity: by default Redwood provides platform-managed keys; however customers can opt for dedicated key provisioning (customer KMS integration) as part of the Dedicated onboarding. If customer-managed keys are requested we document that in the Dedicated contract and provide the KMS integration runbook.
- Private / On-prem: customer-managed keys (no Redwood access) — see rows in the roster flagged "customer-managed".
- Plaintext access: subprocessors listed with 'access_level' = 'plaintext' are small set (hosted logging processor for telemetry redaction pipeline). No subprocessor has access to raw customer content for Private deployments.

Drive link to the same artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/subprocessor-roster-2026-12-21
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/9832 (control mapping attached to the company record).

If you want we can produce an abbreviated controls mapping that references SOC 2 CC and SIG question IDs — Marissa, can you take the SOC 2 controls mapping and drop into a one-page summary for Alice?

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Partner Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
- Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_roster_2026-12-21.csv (CSV)
- Attachment: kms_responsibility_matrix_2026-12-21.pdf (PDF)

Camila / Jonas — thanks for the quick turn. Files look good at a glance and the mapping notes are helpful. Two quick clarifications before we close out the packet:

1) For Dedicated capacity where Redwood provides platform-managed keys by default: who is the operational owner responsible for key rotation — Redwood security ops or the account engineering team? We need a single point of contact for rotation evidence requests during assessment.
2) In your roster CSV you flag one telemetery processor as "plaintext" access — can you confirm whether that access is limited to pseudonymized records or if any downstream service may re-link to identifiers?

If you can reply to those two bullets today that would be great; otherwise we will include the current artifacts and file a short follow-up note in the audit packet.

Best,
Alice Hu
Security Program Manager
MedAlign Health
alice.hu@medalign.com
